# From an acquired response law to later certified control

1 November 2026. Root construction, with a separate mathematical challenge in
`../physical/CONSUMER_REVIEW.md`. All prior Astra premises are pinned to
`51ce47ce39f976517d60e2f87bbe280b651f6056`.

## 1. Physical and information contract

Normalize the admitted fixed response to

    f(x)=h^T P(I+PCP)^(-1)Ph,
    P=diag(sqrt(x)), C>=0, C_ii<=q, |h_i|<=1,
    X={x>=0: sum x_i<=1}.

Its underlying physical gain is F(u)=L f(u/delta), L=delta G^2,
q=delta kappa. A single calibration event supplies an acquired rational
function hatf or the LP interval service with sup_X|hatf-f|<=zeta. Any one
feasible fitted ratio satisfies this when the whole-interval width is <=zeta.
Future commands, prices and constraint sets may be selected after the record.
This is static control of the same fixed source, with the same admissible dose
language. It is not a theorem for unknown evolving dynamics or new actuators.

The later task is to maximize f(x)-c.x over a supplied nonempty compact convex
set K contained in X. The price c is known. K comes with a feasible starting
point and an actual finite-cost linear optimization oracle. No arbitrary
nonconvex planner is assumed. Outputs are an intervention and a regret bound.

## 2. Concavity and curvature belong to the real source

Choose Gram vectors b_i with C_ij=b_i.b_j. They are proof objects, not acquired
data. Woodbury gives

    f(x)=min_z [||z||^2 + sum_i x_i(h_i-b_i.z)^2].        (1)

As the infimum of affine functions of x, f is concave. The minimizing z is
unique because its Hessian in z is positive definite. Put

    A_x=I+sum_i x_i b_i b_i^T, z_x=A_x^(-1)sum_i x_i h_i b_i,
    v_i=h_i-b_i.z_x.

The envelope derivative and its Hessian are

    partial_i f=v_i^2,
    partial_ij f=-2 v_i v_j b_i^T A_x^(-1)b_j.           (2)

Taking z=0 in (1) shows f<=sum x_i h_i^2<=1. Hence ||z_x||<=1,
|v_i|<=1+sqrt(q), and A_x>=I gives

    |partial_ij f|<=2q(1+sqrt(q))^2.                   (3)

Every difference between two points of X has l1 norm <=2. Therefore along
every segment from x to y in X the absolute second derivative is at most

    Ccurv=8q(1+sqrt(q))^2.                            (4)

These bounds include singular C and all dark couplings. The coefficients of
an LP-feasible rational fit need not define a concave function. Only f is
used in (1)--(4).

# Review of the later constrained-control consumer

1 November 2026. Complementary mathematical check of the construction proposed
by the root investigator. This checks the stated finite optimization mechanism;
it is not a review of arbitrary hardware or a claim of optimal oracle complexity.

## Contract

Let the normalized physical response on the full simplex
X={x>=0,sum x_i<=1} be

    f(x)=min_z [ ||z||^2 + sum_i x_i(h_i-b_i^T z)^2 ],
    |h_i|<=1, ||b_i||^2<=q.

The previously acquired record supplies a deterministic function hatf with
sup_X |hatf-f|<=zeta on its simultaneous interval event. Such a hatf can be
one rational feasible pair, using its certified whole-law radius, or the
midpoint of querywise LP intervals. The former needs one fit and subsequent
polynomial evaluations; the latter pays two LP optimizations per value query.
Neither requires a new physical experiment after acquisition.

After seeing the record, a user may choose a nonempty compact convex C subset X,
a known linear price c, a feasible starting point x0 in C, and a linear
optimization oracle over C. The target is max_{x in C} f(x)-c^T x. All costs of
the supplied linear oracle and deployment are charged separately. No nonconvex
feasible set, unknown membership oracle, or physical command implementation is
implicitly supplied.

## Curvature

For the minimizer z_x, ||z_x||^2<=f(x)<=sum x_i h_i^2<=1. Put
v_i=h_i-b_i^T z_x and A=I+sum_i x_i b_i b_i^T. The envelope and derivative
identities are

    partial_i f=v_i^2,
    partial_ij f=-2v_i v_j b_i^T A^(-1)b_j.

Therefore |v_i|<=1+sqrt(q) and every Hessian entry has absolute value at most
beta=2q(1+sqrt(q))^2. For any two points x,v in X, ||v-x||_1<=2, hence

    |(v-x)^T Hess f(y)(v-x)|<=Cq:=8q(1+sqrt(q))^2

along the entire segment. In particular

    f(x+gamma(v-x)) >= f(x)+gamma grad f(x).(v-x)-Cq gamma^2/2.

The inverse A>=I remains regular at boundary points, so no interiority or
eigenvalue-gap assumption is needed.

## Approximate directional oracle from the same record

Let v0=0,v1=e1,...,vn=en denote the full-simplex vertices. At iterate x in C and
step h in (0,1], compute

Concavity plus the curvature bound gives
